notable_absence.finding: cascadesDeletionTo exists in the registry precisely for this shape ('if dropping a scope drops its collections, that is what it is for' - this round's brief), and this page is the single most likely candidate page in the whole corpus to state it: it explicitly covers bucket>scope>collection containment, dropping scopes, dropping collections, and even a special case (default collection droppable, default scope not; _system scope and its collections both non-droppable). Despite all that, the word 'drop' never once appears next to a containment consequence - the page states 'A scope can be dropped' and 'A collection... can be dropped' as isolated facts about each level, never 'dropping a scope drops its collections'. cascadesDeletionTo therefore cannot be minted from this page. This is a real, load-bearing documentation gap, not an extraction failure: an operator reading only this page cannot learn what happens to a scope's collections when the scope itself is dropped.

cross_component_finding: The bullet 'The increased efficiency of indexing, due to the Data Service being able to provide documents from specific collections to the Index Service' is the first page in the registry to state the Data-to-Index-Service relationship in the servesService direction (provider-asserted) rather than the already-promoted dependsOnService direction (consumer-asserted, 'Query Service depends on Index Service and Data Service'). Both predicates now describe overlapping parts of the same three-service chain (Query -> Index -> Data) from opposite ends, which the registry has never connected into one picture.
cross_product_finding: This page defines server:bucket > server:scope > server:collection in Couchbase Server's own words, structurally identical in shape (three-level container hierarchy, same three names) to the already-promoted capella:bucket > capella:scope > capella:collection (recurrence 13/13/14). No page read in this batch, or apparently in nine-plus prior rounds, states that these are the same concept surfaced through two products, or that they are different - per this project's explicit rule, that relationship is NOT invented here. Recorded as a collision needing a human/reconciliation decision, exactly like the registry's existing capella:cluster-manager / capella-role:cluster-manager and four-way 'role' writeups. One data point worth weighing in that decision: capella:collection's own registry note calls it 'a keyspace' - and this server-side page uses 'keyspace path' and 'partial keyspace reference' (n1ql:keyspace-path, n1ql:partial-keyspace-reference, both minted this round) for exactly the same addressing concept, which is suggestive but is a similarity, not a stated identity.
